style.vernacular: Former colonial capital of Burma on the Yangon river delta: a downtown grid of four-storey brick-and-stucco colonial mixed-use blocks (4.3 m ceilings, mezzanines) stained black-green by monsoon mould, surrounded by 6-8 storey walk-up apartment blocks in faded pastel paint with open balconies and rooftop water tanks, 1-2 storey detached houses in the satellite townships under corrugated zinc roofs, and gilded Buddhist stupas rising above leafy tree canopy. No skyscrapers; heights are capped relative to the Shwedagon Pagoda.
style.ornament: Gilded Burmese stupas with bell-shaped domes and tiered finials (hti umbrella); multi-tiered pyatthat roofs and chinthe lions on religious and civic buildings; colonial arched arcades, cast-iron balcony railings and pediments in downtown; mould-darkened stucco; hand-painted signage and tangles of overhead wires.

sources.what: downtown has the most colonial-period buildings in Southeast Asia; mostly four-storey mixed-use buildings with 4.3 m ceilings; 8-storey walk-up apartment blocks; no skyscrapers, height tied to Shwedagon; 1-2 storey houses in satellite towns; tropical monsoon climate
gilded brick stupa, 99 m, gold plates over brick plinth: reference for stupa colouring
1926 colonial market with inner cobblestone streets on the Yangon heritage list
Chinese-Western mixed palace with octagonal tower: example of eclectic Yangon villas
